# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 38 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 38 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_038_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 8 — Abstain from Evil; Practice Good

**1** "Sir, please show me what the evil spirits actually do — I want to recognize their works and stay away from them." **2** "Here is what you must stay away from: evil-speaking, adultery, drunkenness, wicked pleasure, unlawful eating, arrogance and boasting, lying and stealing — and everything like that. **3** Don't think those are small things for a servant of God. Adultery is a serious evil. Drunkenness is a serious evil. Arrogance and boasting are serious evils. These are the great evils that God's servants must avoid. **4** Now hear what you must actively practice. Help widows. Visit orphans and the poor. Rescue God's servants from situations of distress. Be hospitable to strangers. Resist no one. Be humble — in fact, be the most humble and submissive person in the room. Honor the elderly. Live by righteousness. Watch over your love for the brothers and sisters. Endure mistreatment patiently. Hold no grudges. Encourage those who are spiritually sick. Don't write off those who have stumbled in faith — work to restore them and give them courage. Call out sinners where you see them. Don't squeeze money out of debtors and the poor. And everything like this. **5** Are those small things? Not a chance," he said. "They are very great." **6** "Sir, which of these evils am I personally caught in? I want to know so I can turn away from them." "I'll tell you," he said. "Your business dealings — all the transactions and commitments you've taken on — don't let those consume you. Step back from the business and hold on to righteousness instead. **7** Because if you stay entangled in all those business dealings, you won't be able to keep the Lord's commandments. And if you can't keep the Lord's commandments, you won't be saved."

---

*PNEUMA note: The virtue list (v.4) begins with the most vulnerable: widows, orphans, the poor, strangers — a summary of the prophetic social ethics of the Hebrew Bible brought forward into early Christian practice.*
